numerical_failure.observed_behavior: For very small K (e.g. K = 1e-11), exponnorm(K).cdf([-4, 4]) returns [-9.99968e-01, -3.16712e-05] instead of the normal CDF values; cdf values are negative/cancelled. The logpdf also becomes unstable (sudden decrease in predicted log pdf) for K approaching values smaller than 1e-8.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: exponnorm(K).cdf([-4, 4]) should approach the standard normal CDF, i.e. [3.16712e-05, 9.99968e-01] for K = 1e-11; logpdf/cdf/sf should remain accurate as K -> 0 (exponnorm approaches the standard normal).
trigger_conditions: very small shape parameter K (K <~ 1e-9 per commit message; issue reports K = 1e-11 and K approaching values below 1e-8)
evaluation of logpdf, cdf or sf at large-magnitude arguments where the error function suffers cancellation
K values 1e-9, 1e-12 and 1e-15 are the tested regimes in the fix
oracle_clues: Reproducer prints normal CDF and exponnorm CDF side by side with .5e formatting and compares against norm.cdf
Fix tests compare against the standard normal distribution at K = 1e-9, 1e-12, 1e-15

Discussion uses an mpmath high-precision reference (mp_exponnorm_logpdf) with relative error computed where reference exceeds 1e-16; the fix threshold is K < 1 with erfcx branches applied only when u >= 0

numerical_characteristics.precision: 64-bit result precision; intermediate calculations in high precision (mpmath with mp.dps = 75) and only the final result is float
numerical_characteristics.magnitude: Small K: the PR body cites K <~ 1e-9 and the test values are K = 1e-9, 1e-12, 1e-15; the erfcx branch threshold was revised to K < 1 in discussion; the reproducer uses K = 1e-11 with x = [-4, 4], and the discussion's sweep uses x up to +/-1e10
category_specific_evidence: PR body: cancellation in exponnorm.logpdf, cdf and sf for very small K (K <~ 1e-9), fixed with erfcx-based branches.
Issue reproducer: K = 1e-11, x = [-4, 4], compares exponnorm(K).cdf against norm.cdf printed with .5e formatting.
Discussion (issue): for K smaller than about 1e-14 the exponnorm and normal distributions are essentially indistinguishable in float64.
Discussion (issue): the cancellation reduces accuracy of the existing implementation for essentially all K < 1.

Discussion (PR): the reference uses mpmath with mp.dps = 75; relative errors are computed only where the reference exceeds 1e-16 in magnitude, and absolute error for logpdf only where the reference is below 1e16.
Discussion (PR): the mpmath-based tests cover only a small range of K.

Test diff: test_extremely_small_K parametrized over K = 1e-9, 1e-12, 1e-15 with x = [-10.5, -3, -1, 1, 3, 10.5], checking logpdf, cdf and sf against the standard normal using assert_allclose with no explicit rtol or atol.
Commit history: erfcx branch first applied only for K < 1e-6 and u >= 0, then threshold revised to K < 1.
Passages do not state the tolerance at which correct and incorrect answers separate; the 1-ULP claim is not supported by any passage, so tolerance is null.
reproduction_risks: No passage gives an explicit tolerance for the bug-separating comparison; the new test relies on assert_allclose defaults, which are not stated in the passages.
The K threshold changed across commits (1e-9, then 1e-6, then 1), so the regime depends on which revision is repro
